title: What is not a goal of endodontic treatment?
Endodontics Final Exam (Spring 2019): shaping and obturating a canal space that is wide and tapered in the mesio-distal plane
endo: maintaining a coronal and apical seal of the root canal treatment
final: protecting and preserving the remaining tooth structure
column5: providing a supportive and retentive foundation for the placement of a final restoration

title: Evidence and clinical experience suggests that greater tapered rotary instrumentation has\have the following potential disadvantage(s):

endo: inadequate debridement in the thinner, but broader bucco-lingual plane
final: weakens roots
column5: increases the incidence of instrument separation reinforcing procedures that further weaken the roots

title: The advantages of engine-driven 30º oscillating instrumentation include:

title: Treatment for the extrusion of NaOCl beyond the apex does not include
Endodontics Final Exam (Spring 2019): the application of anesthesia and analgesics immediately after the incident
endo: the immediate application of cold compresses
final: the immediate application of hot compresses

title: Steps in avoiding the extrusion of NaOCl over the apex include:

final: assess the canal integrity for signs of perforation or other portals of fluid egress

column6: confirm the identity of the solution prior to irrigation

Narrow, ribbon shaped communication between two canals WITHIN THE SAME ROOT

title: A person with a completely necrotic pulp will many times complain of a lingering pain to cold.
A reversible pulpal inflammation will always give a positive percussion test
Rubber dam isolation should be used during all Endodontic procedures except in situations in which it causes the patient discomfort, in which case a cotton roll isolation is used
Increasing the taper on a file means more dentin will be removed from the canal wall
When filing the MB canal of a lower mandibular molar it is better to use .06 tapered files than .04 tapered files to avoid strip perforation
A tooth with a large PAR (periapical radiolucency) that tests within normal limits to cold is indicative of a diseased pulp
